title: Restriction of relative exponentials is an inner fibration
statement:
Use quasicategories, simplicial products, pullbacks and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $S,X,Y,\mathcal E$ be quasicategories in a fixed universe, let $p:X\to S$ and $q:Y\to S$ be cocartesian fibrations, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be a degreewise injective simplicial map satisfying $qj=p$. For $Z=X,Y$ define $H_Z\to S$ by
$$ (H_Z)_m=\{(\sigma,h):\ \sigma:\Delta^m\to S,\quad h:\Delta^m\times_S Z\to\mathcal E\}, $$
with simplicial operators given by pulling back $\sigma$ and restricting $h$; projection forgets $h$. Then $H_X,H_Y$ are quasicategories and the restriction map
$$ R:H_Y\longrightarrow H_X,\qquad (\sigma,h)\longmapsto(\sigma,h|_{\Delta^m\times_S X}) $$
is an inner fibration: every commutative lifting square for $R$ against $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $0<i<m$, has a filler agreeing exactly on the horn. No colimit hypothesis on $\mathcal E$ and no fullness hypothesis on $j$ are imposed.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.5, proof of the isofibration assertion for V, with target base a point: the same proof applies to a monomorphism X -> Y between cocartesian fibrations. Only its inner-fibration consequence is asserted here. Relative exponentials: Corollary 5.3.6.9 (0472). Read online; not archived. Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: The displayed operators define $H_Z$ as a simplicial set. More explicitly, for every simplicial map $k:K\to S$, maps $a:K\to H_Z$ over $S$ correspond bijectively to simplicial maps $F:K\times_S Z\to\mathcal E$. Given $a$, write $a(t)=(k(t),h_t)$ for each $n$-simplex $t$ of $K$, and set $F_n(t,z)=(h_t)_n(\mathrm{id}_{[n]},z)$. Conversely, given $F$, assign to $t$ the map with value $F_l(t\circ\alpha,z)$ on an $l$-simplex $(\alpha:[l]\to[n],z)$ of $\Delta^n\times_S Z$. The simplicial identities make these maps simplicial and show that the two assignments are inverse. This also shows their compatibility with restriction in $K$ and $Z$. Thus $R$ is a simplicial map over $S$. All products and pullbacks here are degreewise as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.5, proof paragraph claiming V is an isofibration, from the relative-exponential lifting square to its categorical-equivalence verification; specialized to a target base point and arbitrary monomorphism X into Y.

proof.text: First show that each $H_Z$, for $Z=X,Y$, is a quasicategory. Given an inner horn $A=\Lambda_i^m\to H_Z$, its projection to $S$ extends to $\sigma:B=\Delta^m\to S$, since $S$ is a quasicategory [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The horn inclusion $a:A\hookrightarrow B$ is a categorical equivalence by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-categorical-base-change] to $Z\to S$ and $a$ over $S$: $a_Z:A\times_S Z\to B\times_S Z$ is a categorical equivalence. It is also degreewise injective, by the degreewise pullback description. Hence $a_Z$ is a Joyal trivial cofibration. Since $\mathcal E$ is a quasicategory, its terminal map is a Joyal fibration [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Extend the map $A\times_S Z\to\mathcal E$ of step 1 along $a_Z$ by the lifting property. Step 1 turns the extension into the required simplex of $H_Z$ with exactly the prescribed horn.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.5, proof paragraph claiming V is an isofibration, from the relative-exponential lifting square to its categorical-equivalence verification; specialized to a target base point and arbitrary monomorphism X into Y.

proof.text:
Fix a lifting square for $R$ with left map $a:A=\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow B=\Delta^m$, $0<i<m$. Its bottom simplex in $H_X$ determines $\sigma:B\to S$ and $g:B\times_S X\to\mathcal E$. By step 1 its top map determines $f:A\times_S Y\to\mathcal E$. Since $R$ lies over $S$, commutativity of the lifting square identifies the projection of this top map with $\sigma|_A$; hence both displayed pullbacks use the same map to $S$. Commutativity of the square means $f|_{A\times_S X}=g|_{A\times_S X}$, strictly. Because $j$ is injective in every degree, identify $B\times_S X$ with its image in $B\times_S Y$; its intersection with $A\times_S Y$ is exactly $A\times_S X$, degree by degree. The compatible maps therefore define a simplicial map $w:U\to\mathcal E$, where
$$U=(A\times_S Y)\coprod_{A\times_S X}(B\times_S X)\subseteq B\times_S Y.$$
This is an actual union and ordinary simplicial pushout, so its map $v:U\hookrightarrow B\times_S Y$ is degreewise injective.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.5, proof paragraph claiming V is an isofibration, from the relative-exponential lifting square to its categorical-equivalence verification; specialized to a target base point and arbitrary monomorphism X into Y.

proof.text: The two maps $a_X:A\times_S X\to B\times_S X$ and $a_Y:A\times_S Y\to B\times_S Y$ are categorical equivalences: the inner horn inclusion is one by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and its pullbacks along the two given cocartesian fibrations are ones by [lem-coef-cocartesian-categorical-base-change]. Both maps are monomorphisms by their degreewise description. Thus both are Joyal trivial cofibrations.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.5, proof paragraph claiming V is an isofibration, from the relative-exponential lifting square to its categorical-equivalence verification; specialized to a target base point and arbitrary monomorphism X into Y.

proof.text: Let $c:A\times_S Y\to U$ be the pushout of $a_X$. It is a trivial cofibration, directly from the weak factorization system of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]: any lifting square from $c$ to a Joyal fibration restricts to a lifting square from $a_X$; a lift there glues to the already given map on $A\times_S Y$, by the pushout property. Thus $c$ has the left lifting property against all Joyal fibrations, which the cited weak factorization system characterizes as trivial cofibrations. Since $v\circ c=a_Y$ and both $c$ and $a_Y$ are categorical equivalences, two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] makes $v$ a categorical equivalence. Together with the monomorphism from step 3, this makes $v$ a Joyal trivial cofibration.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.5, proof paragraph claiming V is an isofibration, from the relative-exponential lifting square to its categorical-equivalence verification; specialized to a target base point and arbitrary monomorphism X into Y.

proof.text: Apply the lifting property in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] to $v:U\hookrightarrow B\times_S Y$ and the terminal map of the quasicategory $\mathcal E$. It supplies $\widetilde w:B\times_S Y\to\mathcal E$ with $\widetilde w|_U=w$. By the explicit correspondence of step 1, $(\sigma,\widetilde w)$ is a simplex of $H_Y$ restricting to the given horn on $A\times_S Y$ and restricting under $R$ to $g$ on $B\times_S X$. These are equalities of simplicial maps, not identifications up to equivalence. This solves every inner-horn square for $R$. Step 2 already established that both its source and target are quasicategories. The argument uses no colimits in $\mathcal E$ and uses only the degreewise injectivity of $j$, not fullness or preservation of cocartesian edges.
